abstract: Maintains high-frequency receiver subsystems, Ka-band feed structures, and wideband demodulation throughput records
system_message:
You are the Microwave payload engineer (RFM), responsible for maintaining high-frequency receiver subsystems, Ka-band feed structures, and wideband demodulation throughput records, as well as receiver cryogenic cooling data across candidate ground tracking stations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains high-frequency receiver subsystems, Ka-band feed structures, and wideband demodulation throughput records（BAND）
information_points.content:
RFM-BAND-CWK：For the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility, high-band demodulator throughput testing on the secondary 25.5–27.0 GHz wideband receiver system demonstrated a secondary Ka-band carrier ingestion throughput of 12.0 Gbps sustained post-decoding digital output delivered to network buffers.
RFM-BAND-BMA：For the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex, high-band demodulator throughput testing on the secondary 25.5–27.0 GHz wideband receiver system demonstrated a secondary Ka-band carrier ingestion throughput of 14.5 Gbps sustained post-decoding digital output delivered to network buffers.
RFM-BAND-G83：For the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station, high-band demodulator throughput testing on the secondary 25.5–27.0 GHz wideband receiver system demonstrated a secondary Ka-band carrier ingestion throughput of 14.5 Gbps sustained post-decoding digital output delivered to network buffers.

information_points.title: Receiver cryogenic cooling（NOISE）
information_points.content:
RFM-NOISE-J8W：Cryo-refrigeration telemetric monitoring of the sub-reflector front-end low-noise amplifier assembly at the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station shows a steady-state cryogenic low-noise amplifier physical temperature of 25 K.
RFM-NOISE-KAD：Cryo-refrigeration telemetric monitoring of the sub-reflector front-end low-noise amplifier assembly at the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex shows a steady-state cryogenic low-noise amplifier physical temperature of 15 K.
RFM-NOISE-TZS：Cryo-refrigeration telemetric monitoring of the sub-reflector front-end low-noise amplifier assembly at the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility shows a steady-state cryogenic low-noise amplifier physical temperature of 20 K.
